name: Southwest Route / Silver Lake

pitch_detail.notes: Depot Creek Road/trail through old-growth forest; Depot Creek Falls hand-line crossing; international border crossing at Monument 65
Broad talus couloir and stream drainage up to the saddle
pitch_detail.pitch: Ouzel Lake to Silver Lake saddle

pitch_detail.notes: Rightward traverse across heather and moraine slopes at roughly 6,800 ft
Rope up for crevasses; glacier often refrozen and firm in the morning
Short, steep, loose rock gully at the glacier's head to a low col on the southwest ridge
pitch_detail.pitch: Rock gully to SW ridge col

pitch_detail.notes: Short gullies, chimneys, and rock ribs; brief traverse above a remnant snowpatch to the true summit

descent_text: The standard descent simply reverses the ascent line - there is no separate descent route and no rappelling on the Southwest Route. From the summit, downclimb the short scree chute and traverse back across to the east side of the crest, then reverse the short section of Class 2-3 gullies, chimneys, and rock ribs down to the notch/col on the southwest ridge. From the col, downclimb the short, steep, loose rock step back onto the head of the Southwest Glacier and re-rope for glacier travel. Descend the same climber's-right line of 30-40 degree snow/ice, re-crossing (or finding an alternate line around) the marginal snowbridge over the mid-glacier crevasse encountered on the way up - glacier conditions and bridge integrity can change meaningfully between morning ascent and afternoon descent, so reassess rather than assuming the same line is safe. Off the glacier, reverse the traverse across heather and moraine slopes and descend the talus couloir/stream drainage back to Ouzel Lake camp; from there, retrace Depot Creek trail (re-crossing at Depot Creek Falls via the fixed hand-line) back to the Depot Creek Road washout. This is a walk-off/downclimb descent: no fixed rappel anchors exist anywhere on the route per every trip report reviewed - the rope carried is solely for glacier travel and crevasse rescue, not rappelling. The steep, loose rock in the summit gullies and at the glacier-head gully step is the main descent-specific hazard; a party could choose to belay or hand-line a member down the loosest short step near the col if conditions or skill warrant, but this is not standard practice and no such anchor is established.
approach: From the Depot Creek Road washout (~2,600 ft, reached via a rough 4WD spur off Chilliwack Lake Road out of Chilliwack Lake Provincial Park, BC), the hike-in starts on the old roadbed: walk it about 9 minutes to an inconspicuous spur road on the left, follow that spur roughly 4 minutes to a T-junction, then bear right onto an extremely overgrown, sporadically muddy road for about 35 minutes to Monument 65 at the US-Canada border (roughly 45 minutes/0.8 hr total from the washout). From the border the route becomes a crude but discernible climbers' path following Depot Creek through beautiful old-growth forest - easy going where deadfall has been cut out, though dozens of uncut logs remain to step over in places. About 3 miles in, the path reaches Depot Creek Falls, the approach's real crux: crossing wet, slick boulders and slabs at the base of the falls. An old fixed hand-line was still serviceable as of a 2017 NPS trip report and assists at the vertical step here, but it should be treated with caution and backed up if in doubt - this is the approach's primary hazard, especially with a pack on wet rock. Above the falls the path continues through Depot Creek Meadow and Upper Depot Creek to Ouzel (Silver) Lake at roughly 5,700 ft - flat, sandy, mostly treeless benches that serve as the standard base camp for both Spickard and neighboring Mount Redoubt, about 5-6 miles and roughly 6 hours of hiking from the road-end washout; Depot Creek and Ouzel Lake itself provide reliable water throughout. From camp, gain the climbing route by ascending a broad talus couloir and stream drainage north/northeast toward the ~7,200 ft Silver Lake saddle; well before the actual pass, cut right around the toe of a steep rocky buttress into open heather-and-moraine basins and traverse to the toe of the Southwest Glacier, roughly 2.5 hours above camp. Rope up and don crampons/crevasse gear here: the glacier's climber's-right margin offers a line of hard 30-40 degree snow/ice with relatively few crevasses, but roughly halfway up, one distinctly 'inhospitable-looking' crevasse must be crossed on a marginal snowbridge - probe it carefully and be prepared for the bridge to have deteriorated depending on the season. A short, steep, loose rock gully at the glacier's head tops out on the ~8,000 ft col on Spickard's southwest ridge, the start of the summit scramble (easy 3rd-class rock and up to ~35-40 degree snow to the summit ridge).
overview: Mount Spickard is a massive, heavily glaciated peak straddling the Skagit/Fraser drainage divide just 2 miles south of the Canadian border, part of the Chilliwack Group of the Skagit Range. It is the 5th-highest summit in North Cascades National Park and the 16th-highest in Washington, and its roughly 4,779 ft of prominence ranks 9th-greatest in the state. The mountain is built of Tertiary-age gneiss; the Silver Glacier drains north over a mile to Silver Lake, while a separate glacier system on the southwest side extends over 3 miles toward Mount Redoubt. First ascent is credited to Walter B. Reaburn in 1904; the peak's current name was applied in 1963 for climber Warren J. Spickard Jr., who died climbing a nearby peak in 1961. The standard Southwest Route/Silver Lake line climbs broad talus and a southwest glacier to a final short but loose Class 3 rock scramble, and is notable as much for its remote, cross-border approach as for its technical difficulty.
beta: From Ouzel Lake basecamp at 5,640 ft, ascend northeast up broad talus gully toward 7,360 ft pass between Ouzel and Silver Lakes. Veer right onto talus to reach Southwest Glacier; cross glacier carefully avoiding crevasses. Reach 8,000 ft col on south ridge, descend 40 feet, and traverse rightward across open slopes to obvious snow and rock gully. Final approach follows south ridge on right-side until final 100 feet, then cross left for summit. Snow slopes steepen to 35-40 degrees near top.
gear: Rope and full crevasse-rescue kit (harness, prusiks or mechanical ascenders, pickets/screws as conditions warrant)
Helmet (loose rock on the summit gullies/ribs)
Trekking poles for talus, moraine, and brush
Waterproof shell/layer for the Depot Creek Falls hand-line crossing
Bear canister (required/strongly recommended for North Cascades NP backcountry camping)
